project: DWRO S1 — Explicit Remote Placement and Listener Selection
description: Implement story S1 of Direct Worker and Remote Operations by adding persistent root --remote and authored command placement capabilities, dispatching one normalized request through either the local service or exactly the selected --server endpoint without fallback, introducing --listen for local binds with a warned legacy compatibility path, and rejecting documented conflicts with run --with-server and run --with-site.

context.customerAsk: Implement DWRO story S1: persistent root --remote, authored command placement capabilities, endpoint-only --server, new --listen for local listener binds, no silent local fallback, and documented conflicts with run --with-server and run --with-site.
context.problem: The CLI has no explicit execution-placement input and its authored manifest cannot state whether a command is local-only, remote-only, or dual-placement. The global --server flag also selects both HTTP client endpoints and local listener binds, so customers and scripts cannot unambiguously distinguish calling an existing server from hosting one, and unsupported remote requests lack one centralized no-fallback rule.
context.solution: Add persistent root --remote, a resolved local/remote placement value, and per-command placement capabilities to the authored CLI contract. Normalize command inputs once and select exactly one injected local-service or HTTP-client adapter, rejecting unsupported or failed remote placement without fallback. Make --server the remote endpoint selector, add --listen to listener-owning commands, preserve explicit legacy --server binding with a deprecation warning when --listen is absent, give --listen precedence, and enforce documented usage conflicts before side effects.

acceptanceCriteria: The authored CLI manifest defines persistent root --remote, a resolved local/remote placement value, and local-only, remote-only, or dual-placement capabilities for affected commands; executable help and parsing match that contract.

A representative dual-placement operation produces the same normalized request locally without --remote and sends that request to exactly the --server <uri> HTTP endpoint with --remote, with equivalent domain intent across adapters.

Unsupported remote placement, an invalid or unavailable selected server, and remote transport failure return stable actionable errors and never invoke the local product operation, start a listener, or silently select another endpoint.

you server --listen, you run --with-server --listen, and you run --with-site --listen bind the requested local address; when --listen is absent, legacy listener use of an explicitly supplied --server remains functional for the compatibility window and warns, while explicit --listen takes precedence.

--remote with run --with-server or run --with-site is rejected as a documented stable usage conflict before listener, browser, Factory, or remote-operation side effects begin; reference docs and examples use the new placement vocabulary.

Quality gates pass with direct CLI and manifest, package, functional, help and reference, and compatibility evidence as applicable; Typecheck passes, Tests pass, and there are no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared or generated-file churn are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Declare explicit placement in the authored CLI contract
userStories.description: As a CLI user and command implementer, I want root placement and each command's supported placements to be explicit so help, validation, and dispatch share one authoritative contract.
acceptanceCriteria: The authored CLI manifest exposes a visible persistent root --remote boolean whose documented meaning is to execute a supported operation through a running You server; it does not imply async, follow, continuous, or listener behavior.

The executable parser resolves the root input to explicit local placement by default and remote placement when --remote appears before or after the command path, consistent with other persistent flags.

A command can authoritatively declare local-only, remote-only, or dual-placement capability, and manifest validation rejects a runnable command whose placement declaration is missing or invalid where the placement contract applies.

Existing HTTP-only commands retain their historical remote-default compatibility for this window, accept explicit --remote, and do not gain a local implementation merely to satisfy the new vocabulary.
Root and representative command help show the placement meaning and supported usage without describing --remote as a waiting or server-start option.

Focused contract and parser tests prove manifest validation, persistent flag inheritance, before and after command parsing, default placement, and explicit remote placement through observable CLI inputs and help.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Dispatch normalized operations without placement fallback
userStories.description: As a customer, I want the same operation to run locally by default or on exactly my selected server with --remote so placement is predictable and cannot silently change during failure.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one representative supported dual-placement command normalizes customer inputs once before dispatch, calls its already-injected local service adapter without --remote, and calls its HTTP client adapter with --remote.
Behavioral parity coverage proves the local and remote adapters receive contract-equivalent normalized request values for the same customer input, allowing only transport metadata differences.

you --remote --server <uri> <dual-placement-command> sends the operation to exactly <uri> and does not invoke the local product operation, start or probe a local listener, or substitute the default endpoint.
A local-only command invoked with --remote exits with a stable actionable usage error that identifies the unsupported placement before command side effects occur.

Invalid endpoint configuration, connection refusal, timeout, and other remote transport failures remain remote failures and do not retry through the local adapter; diagnostics identify the selected endpoint without leaking credentials or sensitive request content.
Placement selection remains a CLI transport concern: domain services receive normalized operation requests and do not inspect CLI placement flags or discover alternate dependencies.
Focused package and public CLI behavioral tests cover local dispatch, exact remote dispatch, unsupported placement, and failed remote transport with zero local fallback.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented dual-placement `you run` dispatch through one normalized invocation request and an injected local or exact-URI HTTP adapter, with stable unsupported-placement and no-fallback remote errors. Refreshed authored and published CLI contract artifacts and added focused package/public CLI behavioral coverage. Verified with `make contracts-check`, `make cli-manifest-check`, `go test ./pkg/transports/cli/run ./pkg/transports/cli ./pkg/wire ./pkg/services/workers/internal/interface -count=1`, and `make test`; stories 003 and 004 remain outstanding.

userStories.title: Bind local servers with --listen and preserve legacy scripts
userStories.description: As an operator, I want local listener addresses selected with --listen so --server can mean a remote endpoint while my existing listener scripts have a safe migration window.
acceptanceCriteria: you server --listen <address>, you run --with-server --listen <address>, and you run --with-site --listen <address> bind the requested valid local address and report existing stable bind failures for invalid, non-local, or unavailable addresses.
Listener-owning commands use the existing default local bind when neither an explicit --listen nor an explicit legacy bind value is supplied.

During the compatibility window, an explicitly supplied legacy --server <local-uri> continues to select the listener bind only when --listen is absent and emits one actionable deprecation warning on stderr directing the user to --listen.

When both inputs are supplied to a listener-owning command, explicit --listen determines the bind address; --server does not override it, and compatibility diagnostics accurately explain any retained endpoint role.
Ordinary local commands and ordinary you run do not start a listener merely because --listen or the default server endpoint exists; invalid flag placement is rejected before runtime side effects.
CLI manifest relationships, help, and examples describe --listen as the local bind input and --server as the selected You server URI, including the legacy migration behavior.
Focused listener lifecycle tests use observable readiness and bind behavior and prove requested binding, precedence, warning, bind failure, and joined shutdown without arbitrary sleeps.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Reject remote and local-hosting conflicts and publish migration guidance
userStories.description: As a customer, I want contradictory placement modes rejected with clear guidance so the CLI never both calls a remote server and hosts the same run locally.
acceptanceCriteria: you --remote run --with-server and you --remote run --with-site each exit with the same stable usage classification and actionable conflict message, regardless of persistent-flag position.
Conflict validation occurs before Factory execution, HTTP dispatch, listener startup, browser launch, recording, or other run-owned side effects.

Authored CLI relationships, executable help, and packaged reference docs state that --remote selects a running server, --server selects its URI, and --listen selects a local bind; they document both run-mode conflicts and the legacy bind migration.

New customer-facing examples use you --remote --server <uri> for supported remote operations and --listen <address> for local server or server-enabled run binding; they do not present legacy --server listener syntax as the preferred form.
Behavioral CLI tests prove both conflicts, stable exit and error output, zero side effects, and help and reference guidance rather than relying on source or route inventories.
Documentation reference smoke checks pass
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
